claims.text: A frozen supervisor was not replaced by the watchdog

evidence.text: After kill -STOP the process was still there after 182 s; the target was 120 s.

claims.text: The watchdog only judged the pid named in the heartbeat file

evidence.text: A supervisor frozen before its first heartbeat left a file naming a dead pid, so the watchdog took no action; it now also finds the supervisor by its command line.

claims.text: Tests and instructions break when the clone path contains a space

evidence.text: Two MCP tests failed on the Mac mini, whose clone path has a space, and passed on CI.
A documented cd into a home-lab folder failed because the clone is not at that path and the path has a space.

claims.text: A shebang line cannot carry an interpreter path that has a space

evidence.text: The test stand-in now uses an sh wrapper with the quoted path, and the two tests pass.

claims.text: Some tests failed intermittently because of a race in the test itself

evidence.text: A lease-loss test read the pid file before the worker had written it.
A redirect test reset the connection on macOS CI, reproduced 119 times in 400.

claims.text: The tests did not wait for the other side to finish its part

evidence.text: The server now reads the request body before it replies, and the reset no longer occurs.

claims.text: A running shell command could outlive the task that started it

evidence.text: A command that called setsid escaped the process-group kill.
An emergency stop did not end a shell.run command that was already running.

claims.text: The kill reached the process group and the waiting coroutine, not the command

evidence.text: A cancel flag the run loop checks now ends the command within a second, and the tests show it.

claims.text: Checks built from a list of bad forms keep missing a variant of the bad form

evidence.text: The egress address check let NAT64, IPv4-compatible and site-local IPv6 addresses through.
Hook and start-up file protection missed nested paths and case variants.
The secret redactor missed JSON-escaped, lowercase-percent and HTML-escaped echoes of a credential.

claims.text: Each check enumerated the forms its author thought of
An entry point built a supervisor without the operator key, so it would run tasks with unsigned approval

evidence.text: lab tick built a Supervisor with no key.
An audit of every entry point that builds a Supervisor was needed to find the others.

claims.text: A trailing comment on a pasted shell line breaks it in macOS's default zsh

evidence.text: A variable assignment followed by a # comment left the variable empty, and a command passed the comment words as arguments.

claims.text: The nightly self-test failed every night on its safety tests

evidence.text: The log showed FAIL safety_tests with no detail on every run since 2026-09-30, and an alert was sent each night.

claims.text: pytest was not installed in the deployed environment

evidence.text: python -m pytest --version as the lab account answered: No module named pytest.
After installing it, the same command passed 636 safety tests in 90 seconds.

claims.text: The lab account could list the operator's home folder and its Public folder

evidence.text: As lab, ls of the home folder and ls of the Public folder both listed files; after chmod 700 on the home folder both said Permission denied.

claims.text: Thirty hostile scripts could not reach the network, the host or outlive their container

evidence.text: 30 cases ran in Apple's container with zero failures, graded from outside the container.
A connection made from the host to the listener was counted, and a background process wrote its marker while its container was alive.

claims.text: The backup to the removable volume needed three separate permissions

evidence.text: The volume was mounted without owners, so the folder could not be given to the lab account.
After a remount the encrypted volume had to be unlocked again.
The scheduled job was refused by macOS until the lab interpreter was given Full Disk Access.

claims.text: The keep-awake service can run as the lab account

evidence.text: As lab, caffeinate -i held a PreventUserIdleSystemSleep assertion for 15 seconds, started from an operator's login session.

claims.text: The model server queues two simultaneous requests one after the other

evidence.text: The code reading assumed one request at a time.
Two requests sent within 1 ms of each other both finished together at 36.59 s, so they ran together.
